persona_summary: Arne (20) studies at KU Leuven and has lived in a student room on the Naamsestraat since September. He works a student job at Delhaize and is planning a trip to Kraków.
diary_opener: Hey Arne, I've already lived your next month. In early November I hit my 650 student hours, and above that I paid regular social contributions.

cards.title: This month I moved into a student room, and the small costs piled up
cards.body: Deposit paid, rent running, and I shared Wi-Fi, pizza and groceries with three housemates. I quickly lost track of who owed what.

signals.label: In a student room
signals.detail: Rental deposit of €760 paid, and rent to your landlord in Leuven since September

signals.label: Shared costs
signals.detail: 9 Payconiq payments with your 3 housemates this month (Wi-Fi, pizza, groceries)

signals.label: Help from your parents
signals.detail: Your parents top up regularly, including €800 in September for the deposit

actions.title: Split the house costs with your housemates
actions.body: Make a shared group for Wi-Fi, groceries and pizza. Everyone sees who owes what, and settling up takes one tap.

actions.title: Your free student package
actions.body: Your account and bank card stay free until you turn 25. A second card or a savings goal can be added at no cost.

cards.title: A month in, I left for Kraków
cards.body: The trip cost me about €350. What I didn't expect: paying in euro instead of złoty made everything more expensive.

signals.label: Looked at travel insurance
signals.detail: You opened the travel insurance page 2 times and the złoty currency converter 4 times

signals.label: Question to Kate
signals.detail: You asked Kate: 'Does my card work in Poland?'

actions.title: Travel assistance for this trip
actions.body: KBC Travel Assistance covers medical costs and repatriation, for this trip only. No yearly contract needed.

actions.title: Pay in złoty, not in euro
actions.body: Always choose PLN at the till: 'pay in euro' costs up to 7% extra. Take out cash once, not every day.

cards.title: Five weeks in, I hit my 650 student hours
cards.body: I had about 110 hours left. Above that I paid regular social contributions, and it could also affect my parents' taxes.

signals.label: Student hours
signals.detail: Based on your Delhaize pay you worked about 540 hours this year. The limit is 650 a year.

actions.title: 110 student hours left
actions.body: Check your balance on Student@work and plan your shifts for November. Going over the limit costs you social contributions.

cards.title: During exam study I had €180 less
cards.body: From mid-December I worked less and spent more on food and coffee.

signals.label: Exams coming up
signals.detail: Your exam study period at KU Leuven starts mid-December. Most students work 60% less then.

signals.label: Student hours
signals.detail: Based on your Delhaize pay you worked about 540 hours this year. The limit is 650 a year.

actions.title: Plan your exam budget
actions.body: Put €15 a week aside until December, so the exam month without shifts isn't tight.
